cat_gray:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: scientific estimated camera-space depth map for multiview 3D reconstruction.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: an existing transparent 4x4 turntable spritesheet of a ginger voxel cat. Convert it into a registered 4x4 DEPTH BUFFER image of the EXACT SAME CAT VIEWS. Preserve the original silhouette, pose, hook-shaped attached tail, framing, cell layout and camera angles. Do not redesign, round, smooth or reposition any geometry. Output true transparent RGBA outside the original cat shape and through leg/tail gaps.
Primary request: replace ALL material color and illumination with a LINEAR GRAYSCALE encoding of estimated distance toward the viewer. White=nearest visible surfaces, black=farthest visible surfaces, middle gray=the vertical rotation axis through the center of the cat's torso. This is Z depth, NOT grayscale photography, clay shading, normals, AO, edge highlighting, or surface lighting. Ginger stripes, cream paws, green eyes and pink ears must NOT survive as color/brightness patterns; only actual geometric relief may change the grayscale. On each flat voxel face parallel to the image plane the gray value must be constant. Surfaces farther from the camera are darker regardless of their orientation or material.
Use ONE fixed linear depth scale for ALL 16 frames: let H=cat height from paws to ear tips; gray 0 represents signed camera depth -0.6 H, gray 128 represents depth 0 at the rotation center, gray 255 represents depth +0.6 H toward the viewer. Do NOT auto-normalize each frame separately. The front muzzle should be near/light in front views and the tail far/dark; in rear views the tail should be near/light and the hidden muzzle far. In side views the near legs are lighter than the far legs.
Camera views are unchanged row-major front, 25,45,68,90,120,145,165,180,210,235,255,270,300,320,340 degrees, 5 degree elevation. Use smooth grayscale depth transitions only where actual surface depth changes. Maintain voxel steps and all four paws and the full tail.
Constraints: no illumination, cast shadows, highlights, outlines, color, legends, text, numbers, grid lines, ground plane, or extra objects. Transparent background. The output is a depth measurement hypothesis that will be decoded numerically, so geometric correspondence and consistent depth values matter more than artistic appearance.
cat_color:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: registered FALSE-COLOR camera Z-depth spritesheet, not a beauty render.
Input image 1 is the exact EDIT TARGET, a 4-column 2-row sheet with 8 views of the same voxel cat. Preserve its 8 cat silhouettes, cell layout, rest poses, camera angles, scale, paws and hooked tail pixel-for-pixel as closely as possible. Do not redesign the cat. Transparent alpha background.
Replace every material with an UNLIT FALSE COLOR computed ONLY from depth toward the camera. This should resemble a scientific depth buffer, NOT a colorful lit sculpture. Remove stripes, eye pigments, cream muzzle, paw colors and pink ears as material features. Geometric eye recesses and nose relief remain only as depth differences.
Depth palette, same absolute scale for ALL 8 panels: far=-0.6 cat heights from torso rotation center is pure blue (#0000FF); depth=-0.3H is cyan (#00FFFF); center depth=0 is pure green (#00FF00); depth=+0.3H is yellow (#FFFF00); near depth=+0.6H is pure red (#FF0000). Interpolate through those colors (HSV hue 240 degrees far to 0 degrees near). NO lighting or ambient occlusion. Flat front-facing voxel faces have uniform hue; surfaces at the same Z-depth have the same hue regardless of orientation or original paint color.
Most visible surfaces should be green/yellow/orange rather than blue, because they lie in front of the center; the tail visible behind the cat in FRONT views must be cyan/blue, and the same tail in BACK views must be yellow/orange/red. Near-side paws have warmer hue than far-side paws. Do not color the top of the tail white; use its Z-depth hue. Concavities such as the gap inside the tail curl and leg openings are genuinely transparent, not a color.
View order left to right: top row front 0 degrees, front-left45, left profile90, left-rear145. Bottom row rear180, rear-right235, right profile270, right-front320. Camera elevation5 degrees. The camera rotates; the cat stays in exactly one fixed pose.
Output exactly 4 columns by 2 rows, no labels, outlines, grid, scale bars, checkerboard, captions, beauty lighting, shadows, or other objects. Preserve transparency, the hooked tail volume and all four paws. This map will be numerically unprojected into 3D, so absolute consistency of hue and geometry across panels is essential.
control:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: camera-space Z-depth buffer conversion of existing game model renders.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: a 4-column by 2-row transparent contact sheet rendered from two real 3D assets, top row a cat and bottom row an adventurer. Convert EXACT existing visible geometry to false-color depth. Do not beautify or repair either model, including their imperfect voxel surfaces. Preserve all silhouettes, poses, layout, pixel positions, scale and camera angles. Row-major each row shows front, left profile, rear, right profile. Orthographic camera elevation5 degrees, +Y up, character height approximately one unit.
Return an identically registered 4x2 true-transparent sheet. Replace ALL material/lighting colors with depth hue. No shading, highlights, occlusion shading, outlines or paint markings.
Depth definition: signed distance TOWARD the camera from the vertical rotation axis through the center of each model. Use the SAME range across all eight cells: depth -0.6 heights=blue RGB(0,0,255), -0.3=cyan(0,255,255), 0=green(0,255,0), +0.3=yellow(255,255,0), +0.6=red(255,0,0). Interpolate hue blue-to-red by decreasing HSV hue from240 to0, saturation1,value1. Do not map distance from the floor or image left/right to hue. Do not normalize per panel.
All foreground surface points with identical depth get identical hue irrespective of their original material. Flat voxel faces facing the viewer are uniform colors, not lit facets. The gray/cream paw markings do not become orange bands unless geometry depth changes. Front cat muzzle is near/warm, rear cat tail is near/warm; in side views nose and tail mainly differ horizontally, NOT necessarily in depth, and therefore should have similar hues to other surfaces on the same near side of the cat. On the adventurer, visible backpack is warm in the rear view and cool where behind her in the side views. Holes and all background have alpha0.
This is a numerical geometry measurement experiment. Return only the depth sheet, with no other objects, text, legend, labels, background, ground plane or shadows. Exact shape correspondence and consistent metric depth colors are essential.
